data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["SRC_007 concerns subjective perceptual judgment in checklist items vs. objectively verifiable outcomes, whereas this claim concerns objective outcomes with variable difficulty","SRC_007's difficulty analysis may require calibration curves; this claim uses a simpler interaction test that is feasible within a single evaluation if difficulty is ex ante measurable"],"overturn_conditions":["Difficulty cannot be operationalized ex ante within a single evaluation, making the interaction untestable","The interaction between difficulty and accuracy differential is not monotonic, complicating the discrimination","The expert's reliability also decreases with difficulty at the same rate as the panel's, eliminating the differential interaction"],"shared_structure":["Both involve distinguishing genuine reliability from tracking the right answer via difficulty-dependent analysis","Both require item-level variation in difficulty within a single evaluation"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_007"],"transfer_claims":["The difficulty \u00d7 accuracy-differential interaction is the single-evaluation discriminator between aggregation-driven reliability and coverage-coincidence","Genuine reliability gain is difficulty-amplifying; mere compliance is difficulty-attenuating","The interaction test is feasible within a single evaluation if difficulty is operationalized ex ante"]},"claim":"Whether a panel of non-experts with a checklist outperforms a single expert depends entirely on the joint distribution of task difficulty and checklist coverage: for tasks where the checklist's features are necessary and sufficient, the panel wins via error aggregation; for tasks where the checklist is insufficient, the expert wins via tacit knowledge. A single evaluation distinguishes the two regimes by testing for an interaction between item difficulty and panel-vs-expert accuracy differential: a genuine reliability gain manifests as the panel's advantage increasing with difficulty (because aggregation suppresses the harder-to-judge errors), while mere checklist compliance manifests as the panel's advantage being constant or decreasing with difficulty (because harder items exceed checklist coverage).","counterconditions":[{"case":"Task difficulty is not measurable ex ante within a single evaluation, making the interaction untestable","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is equally sufficient across all difficulty levels, meaning there is no interaction to detect","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Difficulty interacts with expert reliability in the same direction as it interacts with panel reliability, masking the differential effect","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Task difficulty and checklist coverage interact. Easy items are within checklist coverage, so both panel and expert succeed. Hard items may exceed checklist coverage, so the expert's tacit knowledge advantage grows while the panel's shared checklist-induced bias dominates. The interaction between difficulty and accuracy differential is the single-evaluation signature: if the panel's advantage grows with difficulty, aggregation is doing work (genuine reliability gain); if the panel's advantage shrinks or reverses with difficulty, the checklist is merely tracking easy cases (compliance coincidence). This interaction is observable within a single evaluation if items vary in difficulty and difficulty can be operationalized ex ante (e.g., by feature ambiguity, base rate, or inter-rater agreement on a gold-standard subset).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
